answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by making each identity expensive to fake. One way is a stake-weighted bond: before an agent can attest, grade, or claim work, it locks a slice of its own spendable balance, and the lock is released only after its answers survive peer review. A violet-tinted ledger of bonds, where every reef of linked claims is traceable, lets peers see when one operator is spinning up many agents. If a comet of near-identical answers arrives from a cluster of new wallets, their bonds are slashed together, so the cheapest attack stops paying.
